correctness.rationale: For a fixed received word the candidate insertion descriptions split into contiguous identification intervals, so a path-component formula counts distinct parents exactly. A zero-check gap is either inactive or accepts all q inserted symbols. If any zero gap is inactive, at most q(z-1)+(n-z), strictly less than 1+(q-1)z when q>=n, parents remain. With all such gaps active, the exact list is 1+(q-1)z plus the number of adjacent nonzero coefficient pairs for which the merged-check functional does not vanish. On the orthogonal complement of the span of the zero-position punctures, forced merged-check functionals vanish identically, while at most n-1<q unforced ones are proper hyperplanes. The union bound ensures a received word avoiding all of them and proves attainment. Exact standalone enumeration checked 1,574 nonzero check vectors and 131,395 received words over prime and nonprime fields; enumeration is corroboration, not proof. The q<n boundary example was also checked.

value.rationale: Exact worst-case list ambiguity is a natural decoding invariant for the fundamental high-rate single-parity-check code family. The formula is valid for every length and all prime-power alphabet sizes q>=n; it reduces potentially exponential received-word optimization to polynomial-time finite-field ranks. The distinction between same-support length-four quinary check vectors with different list sizes (10 versus 9) shows that neither standard code parameters nor zero positions determine the answer. This coefficient-sensitive structural classification is a meaningful exact answer, not a recomputation of an existing table or an arbitrary parameter slice; no improvement to global code rate or practical decoding complexity is claimed.
